conventions.convention: Worldline entries are future timelike and parametrized by proper time, with g(U,U) = −c²; ray entries are smooth, future null and affinely parametrized.
The frequency-ratio readout is E_R/E_E; redshift is z = E_E/E_R − 1.
Data records declare closed boxes with nonnegative hard bounds; they supply no sampling law, coverage probability or statistical inference. Consistency requires a separately declared comparison rule.

Deflection uses a supplied observer-preserving Lorentz isometry between tangent spaces and principal arccos with values in [0,π]. Perihelion advance uses a supplied continuous unwrapped azimuth and subtracts one positive circuit, even for negatively oriented traversal.
The reciprocal-window lemma assumes a_* > 0 and 0 < u_1 ≤ u_2; coincident endpoints give a singleton window of zero length.

The example fixes the flat vacuum exponential datum with H > 0 and Λ = 3H²/c², parameter set (0,a_R), and illustrative redshift box [1/2,3/4]. Scale factors are in metres, times and the affine parameter in seconds, and redshift is dimensionless.

load_bearing.statement: An operational model is a tuple (S,Θ,θ,D,F), with S and Θ nonempty, θ:S→Θ surjective, configurations D(s), and F:Θ→R^d satisfying interpretation (*): its components are the corresponding framework readouts for those configurations under the cited hypotheses. Data records declare closed boxes; comparison claims require their own rule.

For a_* > 0, F(a)=a_*/a is a strictly decreasing bijection (0,∞)→(0,∞), with inverse u↦a_*/u. For 0<u_1≤u_2, F⁻¹([u_1,u_2])=[a_*/u_2,a_*/u_1], of length a_*(u_2−u_1)/(u_1u_2), positive exactly when u_1<u_2.

The explicit exponential flat-vacuum ray yields an operational redshift model F(a_E)=a_R/a_E−1 on (0,a_R). Under the declared illustrative record and comparison rule, its consistency set is [4a_R/7,2a_R/3], of exact length 2a_R/21.

concerns.concern: Clause (a) restricts configuration entries to objects of the listed kinds, but clause (b)3 requires D to contain an isometric identification Φ:T_{p_1}M→T_{p_2}M. No listed entry kind admits such a linear map. A finite real parameter tuple could encode a matrix only after additional chart/basis and reconstruction conventions, which are not supplied. The deflection slot therefore needs an explicit admissible identification entry or a clarification that Φ is separately supplied readout data.

Clause (b)3 calls q_i=h_{n_i}(W(s_i)) 'the spatial projection of clause (b) of def-gr-observer-and-rest-space'. That supplier's clause (b) defines the rest space; its clause (c) defines spatial projection. The formula is correct, but the exact citation locator is wrong.

seams_checked.note: The cosmological redshift theorem is identified as a conditional prediction for comoving observers, not as measured evidence.
The strain slot retains the prescribed finite-path ideal-detector definition and distinguishes it from apparatus, optical readout, calibration and noise modelling.
Stationary redshift is restricted to static exterior observers; circular-orbit predictions are not restated as eccentric perihelion-advance predictions.
Smooth time-oriented Lorentzian geometry, the metric-selected connection and SI conventions are retained without empirical claims.
Proper-time normalization and affine null-geodesic conventions agree with the suppliers; clock and light-ray rules remain adopted physical assumptions.
Observer normalization, projection, positive-definite rest spaces and positive observer energies are used faithfully. The projection clause locator has the presentation defect recorded in concerns.

The exponential datum satisfies the de Sitter theorem's flat vacuum hypotheses with Λ=3H²/c². The constructed future affine null ray satisfies the cosmological redshift theorem's hypotheses, giving 1+z=a_R/a_E.
The geometry and connection conventions are preserved, and dimensional declarations make Hs and the logarithm argument dimensionless.
With U=∂_t and n=U/c, the interface energy −g(W,U) equals the cosmological theorem's −c g(W,n).

Comoving curves have cosmic time as proper time up to origin. The explicit ray satisfies every affine geodesic equation; its physical light-ray interpretation is conditional on the adopted geometric-optics rule.
